title: Scheduler Health Oracle and Self‑Heal Procedures
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines the Scheduler Health Oracle (SHO) — an auditable, real‑time decision layer that monitors kernel/scheduler health, synthesizes signals across layers, and executes pre‑approved self‑heal actions. The goal is to reduce noisy oncall interrupts for transient kernel noise while providing rapid, reversible remediation for deterministic faults that threaten SLOs.

Audience:
- Oncall SREs and runtime engineers
- Kernel and scheduler owners
- Runtime observability and automation engineers

Why SHO: problem statement
- Scheduler-level regressions (priority inversion, admission spikes, kernel starvation) often manifest across multiple signals with non-obvious causality.
- Manual triage is slow; highly-automated remediation must be conservative, observable, and reversible.
- The SHO provides a standard decision contract and safe remediation actions so teams can opt-in with clear guardrails.

High-level design
1) Signal ingestion: aggregated telemetry from dispatcher, kernel-profiles, KVCache, GPU telemetry, and network layer.
2) Feature synthesis: rolling-error rates, kernel latency percentiles, credit-accounting deltas, slot utilization, and memory pressure indices.
3) Heuristic and ML tiers: short ruleset-based checks for high-confidence faults + an optional ML model to identify correlated multi-signal anomalies.
4) Policy engine: maps detected failure modes to approved remediation actions with associated confidence thresholds.
5) Actuation/blocking: dry-run, non-blocking notification, or automatic remediation. All actions are logged to the incident trace and can be rolled back automatically or manually.

Detection signals and thresholds (baseline)
- kernel_cpu_latency_p50/p95/p99 (per-kernel): p95 > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive 1m buckets => medium severity
- scheduler_queue_depth: sustained > 85% of configured capacity for 2m => medium
- kernel_preemptions_rate: increase > 3x baseline => high
- slot_evictions_per_min: > 10/min for a node cohort => medium
- kvcache_warmup_failures: 5 failures within 5m => low
- gpu_thermal_throttle: any non-transient throttle event logged by NVML => high
- cross-signal rule: if p99 latency increase + scheduler_queue_depth spike + kernel_preemptions_rate rise => immediate canary rollback action at confidence >= 0.8

Policy mapping examples
- High-confidence GPU thermal throttle (NVML): immediate isolate node (cordon + drain policy) => action: schedule node cordon, redirect new requests, start evacuation.
- Kernel preemption storm (rule-based): lower background priority cohort for 2m, enable cooperative preemption mode => action: toggle scheduler param preempt_coop=true for affected cohort.
- Latency increase with KV cache misses: enable KV prefetch hints + increase warm pool size by +10% for 10m.
- Admission overload (queue depth): enable temporary token-based backpressure: set admission.max_inflight to 70% of baseline for 5m.

Runbook: automated remediation decision flow
1. Detection: SHO raises an event with reason_code and confidence score.
2. Verification: SHO attempts a secondary verification sampler (shadow query of kernel health; targeted microtraces) — 30s.
3. Mode selection: 
a) Confidence >= 0.9 and matches high-impact rule => automatic remediation with full audit.
b) Confidence between 0.6 and 0.9 => gated remediation: perform non-blocking action (e.g., param tweak plus page to oncall) and run 5m watch.
c) Confidence < 0.6 => create incident page and alert, no actuation.
4. Actuation: perform action using orchestration API (see Actuation API spec snippet below).
5. Observe: track remediation effect via pre and post windows (1m, 5m, 10m).
6. Rollback: if metrics do not improve or regress further, automatically revert parameter and mark as failed remediation.
7. Postmortem: automatically create an incident skeleton and assign to the owning team if confidence >= 0.6 and an action was taken.

Actuation API: example cURL and YAML policy (safe defaults)
- cURL (sample):

curl -X POST https://orchestrator.internal/api/v1/actuate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SHO_TOKEN' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"action":"tweak_scheduler_param","target":"cohort:gpu-rt-*-west","params":{"preempt_coop":"true","duration":"300s"},"correlation_id":"sho-20261102-1234"}'

- Policy YAML (human-editable):

policy_id: sho_default_2026
description: Conservative remediation policies for scheduler-level faults
rules:
  - id: cordon_on_gpu_thermal
    selectors: ["gpu_thermal_throttle==true"]
    confidence_threshold: 0.9
    action:
      name: cordon_node
      params: {drain_timeout: 120, evac_cohort: gpu-rt-*}
  - id: coop_preempt_during_preempt_storm
    selectors: ["kernel_preemptions_rate>3x"]
    confidence_threshold: 0.8
    action:
      name: tweak_scheduler_param
      params: {preempt_coop: true, duration: 300}

Observability and dashboards
- SHO Dashboard (Grafana):
  - Primary row: composite SHO confidence time-series, active remediations, last_revert_time.
  - Signal heatmap: per-cluster kernel p99, queue depth, preemption_rate.
  - Action audit log: rendered list of actuations with correlation_id and link to incident page.

- Tracing: all SHO decisions attach a correlation_id (sho-<date>-<seq>) to traces. Use the tracing explorer to filter traces by correlation_id.

Oncall playbook (quick steps)
1. Page received with action_id and correlation_id. Immediately check SHO dashboard link; confirm whether the action was automatic or gated.
2. If an automatic action executed: verify the pre/post metric windows.
   - If improvement within 2 windows (5/10m) -> mark incident as mitigated and start RCA.
   - If no improvement -> press the "revert" button in the SHO UI; revert executes immediate rollback and creates a hotfix ticket.
3. If it was a gated action: follow the remediation recommendation, but use the orchestrator-console to perform a controlled manual action instead of automatic.
4. If GPU node cordoned: confirm evacuation succeeded and note impacted customers; follow customer notification template (appendix).
5. After action: run short hypothesis test (see Appendix B) and annotate the incident with the traced signals used by SHO.

Safety and guardrails
- All automated actuations are rate-limited: max 2 concurrent cluster-wide automated actions per 10m.
- Any actuation that affects routing (fallback to variant models, cross-region shift) requires emergency-owner approval and cannot be automatically initiated.
- A signed audit entry with operator and source (SHO vs manual) must exist for all actuations.
- All policy changes must pass a canary in the staging fleet for 48h before being promoted to production.

Testing the SHO in staging (step-by-step)
1. Deploy SHO snapshot to staging cluster with policy sho_staging_2026.
2. Seed synthetic traffic with a controlled preemption spike using the stress-injector: 
   ./tools/stress-injector --target cohort=gpu-rt-staging --preempt-rate=5x --duration=120s
3. Verify SHO detected event and logged dry-run actuation.
4. Promote to gated mode and validate that a param tweak was recommended but not auto-applied.
5. Promote to auto-mode for non-destructive actions (e.g., increasing warm pool size) only after 48h.

Operational telemetry to collect (minimum)
- sho.decisions.count (by outcome: dryrun, gated, auto, revert)
- sho.decision_confidence.histogram
- sho.action_latency_ms (time between decision and actuation)
- kernel.latency.p99 (per-kernel, per-cohort)
- scheduler.queue_depth.percentile (1m, 5m)
- orchestrator.action_success_rate and revert_rate

Post-incident process and RCA guidance
- If SHO action was involved in mitigation, the RCA must include: decision rationale, confidence score, pre/post graphs, and audit correlation_id.
- Use the RCA template: Summary, Timeline, Hypothesis, Evidence (graphs/traces), Root cause, Mitigation, Long-term fix, Owner, ETA.

Appendix A: Example incident annotations (paste into incident page)
- sho:correlation_id: sho-20261102-1234
- sho:policy: sho_default_2026
- sho:decision: coop_preempt_during_preempt_storm
- sho:confidence: 0.87
- pre-window: kernel.p99=48ms -> post-window: 22ms

Appendix B: Hypothesis quick-tests
1. Isolate: reproduce the kernel preemption spike in staging with identical workload shapes.
2. Swap: reroute a small traffic cohort to an alternate scheduler variant and measure p99 delta.
3. Harden: apply the param tweak in a canary cohort and run a 1-hour stress profile.

Appendix C: Customer notification template (if nodes evacuated)
- Subject: Temporary capacity change in <region> (date/time)
- Body: We detected elevated thermal events affecting a subset of nodes and routed traffic to healthy capacity. No data exposure is suspected. We are monitoring and will update when all nodes are rejoined.

Appendix D: Common CLI commands and quick checks
- sho-status: show active SHO decisions
  $ shoctl status --cluster=us-west --format=table
- list recent actuations
  $ shoctl actions --since=1h --limit=50 --cluster=us-west
- revert an action manually
  $ shoctl revert --action-id=act-20261102-9876 --reason="no improvement"
